x-inspectra.cliParsedDescription: Vericairn: records, estates and the tools that keep them honest.

options.name: --help
options.description: Show help and usage information

options.name: --version
options.description: Show version information

options.name: --estate
options.description: Path to the estate repository root. [default: <path>]

options.name: --json
options.description: Machine-readable output. [default: False]

options.name: --recipient
options.description: The person addressed by human presentation (ULID); omitted means estate defaults, never an inferred person.

options.name: --for-assignment
options.description: Exact assignment for the recipient's communication override.

options.name: --depth
options.description: One-view depth: short, standard or comprehensive. Canonical --json is independent of depth.

commands.name: communication
commands.description: Inspect or change attributable personal communication settings. Remote is not built.

commands.name: show
commands.description: Show effective values, contributing revisions, conflicts and freshness.

options.name: --preview
options.description: Show the shared status, decision, result and handoff examples. [default: False]

commands.name: set
commands.description: Change the named fields, preserving the others; inherit resets a field.

options.name: --as
options.description: Actual author; defaults to their own setting unless --recipient names another person.

options.name: --scope
options.description: person, estate, or assignment (also selected by --for-assignment). [default: person]

options.name: --expected
options.description: Expected prior revision hash, or absent to require no existing profile. Without it the command reads the current revision before applying the named fields.

options.name: --authority
options.description: Explicit communication-delegation record for a delegated change.

options.name: --basis
options.description: Exact decision being explicitly adopted; does not grant delegated authority.

options.name: --progress
options.description: none, completion-and-need, milestones, verbose, or inherit.

options.name: --status
options.description: short, standard, comprehensive, or inherit.

options.name: --decisions
options.description: Decision lead depth, or inherit.

options.name: --results
options.description: Result explanation depth, or inherit.

options.name: --handoffs
options.description: Handoff introduction depth, or inherit.

commands.name: reset
commands.description: Reset this complete scope to inheritance as a new record.

options.name: --as
options.description: Actual author; defaults to their own setting unless --recipient names another person.

options.name: --scope
options.description: person, estate, or assignment (also selected by --for-assignment). [default: person]

options.name: --expected
options.description: Expected prior revision hash, or absent to require no existing profile. Without it the command reads the current revision before applying the named fields.

options.name: --authority
options.description: Explicit communication-delegation record for a delegated change.

options.name: --basis
options.description: Exact decision being explicitly adopted; does not grant delegated authority.

options.name: --progress
options.description: none, completion-and-need, milestones, verbose, or inherit.

options.name: --status
options.description: short, standard, comprehensive, or inherit.

options.name: --decisions
options.description: Decision lead depth, or inherit.

options.name: --results
options.description: Result explanation depth, or inherit.

options.name: --handoffs
options.description: Handoff introduction depth, or inherit.

commands.name: delegate
commands.description: Explicitly grant or revoke changes to one's own communication setting; grants no other permission.

options.name: --as
options.description: The recipient granting consent.

options.name: --to
options.description: The delegated principal.

options.name: --revoke
options.description: Revoke the current delegation. [default: False]

options.name: --expected
options.description: Expected prior delegation hash; required when revising a grant.

options.name: --expires
options.description: Expiry as a UTC record timestamp.

commands.name: records
commands.description: Create, validate, describe and format records.

commands.name: validate
commands.description: Parse and validate every record and the manifest of an estate.

commands.name: new
commands.description: Create a record in canonical form, validate the estate with it, and write it.

options.name: --by
options.description: Authoring principal id (ULID).

options.name: --body
options.description: Path to a JSON file holding the body, or '-' for standard input.

options.name: --subject
options.description: Subject as type:id or type:id:hash.

options.name: --supersedes
options.description: Id of the record this one replaces.

options.name: --at
options.description: Authoring time, for example 2026-10-13T14:00:00Z (default: now).

options.name: --id
options.description: Explicit record id; only the root operator principal needs this.

commands.name: show
commands.description: Read one complete original record by id; presentation depth never changes it.

commands.name: describe
commands.description: Explain record types and their fields.

arguments.name: TYPE
arguments.description: Record type to describe; omit to list all types.

commands.name: format
commands.description: Rewrite record files in canonical pretty form without changing their content or hash.

arguments.name: FILES
arguments.description: Record files to rewrite in canonical pretty form.

commands.name: hash
commands.description: Print the computed content hash of a record file.

commands.name: estate
commands.description: Create and check estates.

commands.name: init
commands.description: Create a new estate: operator principal, charter and manifest, validated together.

options.name: --profile
options.description: Storage profile: repository-synced (records as files in a git repository) or local-only (records in this machine's live store). [default: repository-synced]

options.name: --name
options.description: Estate display name.

options.name: --slug
options.description: Estate slug (lower-case kebab-case).

options.name: --purpose
options.description: Why the estate exists.

options.name: --operator-name
options.description: Display name of the root operator (a human).

options.name: --organization
options.description: Organization display name.

options.name: --github
options.description: GitHub organization login, if any.

options.name: --repository
options.description: GitHub owner/name of the Vericairn source to pin. [default: Vericairn/vericairn]

options.name: --commit
options.description: Commit of the Vericairn source to pin (40 hex digits).

commands.name: check
commands.description: Validate records and run repository cleanliness and portability checks. Warn when the manifest pins a release below a newer published release known from this estate's release records or the machine-local cache; use vericairn estate upgrade to review and apply an upgrade. This command makes no release-check request, and a newer-release warning never changes its exit code to an error.

commands.name: export
commands.description: Write a verified export: records, objects, manifest and documents with an inventory; no keys or authority.

options.name: --out
options.description: Path of the export file to create (never overwritten).

options.name: --by
options.description: Principal id recorded as the exporter.

commands.name: restore
commands.description: Verify an export against its inventory and restore it into an empty directory as a repository-synced estate; authority is not restored.

options.name: --from
options.description: Export file.

options.name: --to
options.description: Empty destination directory.

commands.name: upgrade
commands.description: Pin the estate to a published release and apply record-format migrations as one reviewable change with a migration record.

options.name: --to
options.description: Version of a published release recorded in this estate.

options.name: --by
options.description: Principal id applying the upgrade (required unless --check).

options.name: --check
options.description: Show the plan without changing anything. [default: False]

commands.name: reconcile
commands.description: List what two diverged copies left to settle: divergent revisions, duplicate keys, duplicate results.

commands.name: work
commands.description: Briefs, assignments, attempts, results and amendments of work orders.

commands.name: brief
commands.description: Export the brief of a work order: everything a contributor needs, from the records alone.

arguments.name: WORK_ORDER
arguments.description: Work-order key (for example M1-WORK) or record id.

commands.name: assign
commands.description: Delegate a work order to a contributor under a brief, pinned to the exact work-order revision.

options.name: --contributor
options.description: Principal id of the contributor the work is delegated to.

options.name: --by
options.description: Authoring principal id (ULID).

options.name: --brief
options.description: Path to a JSON file holding the brief (outcome, sources, permittedChanges, prohibitedEffects, workspace, limits, expectedOutputs, reviewCriteria, recovery), or '-' for standard input.

options.name: --note
options.description: Free text.

arguments.name: WORK_ORDER
arguments.description: Work-order key (for example M1-WORK) or record id.

commands.name: attempt
commands.description: Record the start of an attempt by the assignment's contributor.

options.name: --by
options.description: Authoring principal id (ULID).

options.name: --workspace
options.description: Where the work happens, named without machine paths (a repository and branch, a clone, a tool).

options.name: --note
options.description: What the contributor intends to do.

options.name: --at
options.description: Start time, for example 2026-10-13T14:00:00Z (default: now).

commands.name: result
commands.description: Submit the result of an attempt: outcome, summary, outputs by hash, evidence, checks, limitations, unresolved effects, next step.

options.name: --by
options.description: Authoring principal id (ULID).

options.name: --body
options.description: Path to a JSON file holding the body, or '-' for standard input.

commands.name: amend
commands.description: Request a change to an assignment's outcome, scope, target, budget or permitted effects; it authorizes nothing.

options.name: --by
options.description: Authoring principal id (ULID).

options.name: --body
options.description: Path to a JSON file holding the body, or '-' for standard input.

commands.name: takeover
commands.description: Take over a step an agent holds: the hand-over is a new assignment of the step to a person, carrying the agent's brief and naming the agent's assignment, which holds the step from then on; every run of the agent's assignment still in flight is asked to stop. A person records it, the one taking the step over, the sponsor of its goal or an operator, never an agent.

options.name: --by
options.description: Authoring principal id (ULID).

options.name: --contributor
options.description: The person who takes the step over; the recording principal when omitted.

options.name: --note
options.description: Why; a sentence naming the hand-over when omitted.

commands.name: observe
commands.description: Show a work order's assignments, attempts, results, amendments, reviews and acceptances.

arguments.name: WORK_ORDER
arguments.description: Work-order key (for example M1-WORK) or record id.

commands.name: goal
commands.description: Goals: objectives the estate carries out, done when their record predicates hold, an evaluator who did none of the work finds every condition met, and they are accepted. Without a subcommand, the current goal condition by condition: the one goal neither achieved nor ended, or with none or several, the list.

commands.name: show
commands.description: Show a goal condition by condition: its status, the budget its activation grants, each condition's verdict with the records it read beside its current evaluation's, its steps, and what stands between it and its acceptance.

arguments.name: GOAL
arguments.description: Goal record id (any revision); omit for the current goal.

commands.name: next
commands.description: Show a goal's next steps routed from this machine: each eligible step with the principal its role's roster reaches (an agent where a launcher for its harness, its admitted key and the goal's budget allow, a person where needed, a reserved action only to one who holds it) or why none is available, whether the goal's budget allows it, and what holds the others. It records and starts nothing; vericairn goal step takes the next one.

arguments.name: GOAL
arguments.description: Goal record id (any revision); omit for the current goal.

commands.name: propose
commands.description: Propose a goal, or a revision of one: what done looks like, its constraints, its budget and its sponsor. A proposal authorizes and funds nothing. Anyone may propose a goal; a revision is its sponsor's when the sponsor is a person, and an operator's when an agent sponsors it, and anyone else proposes the change as an ask.

options.name: --by
options.description: Acting principal id (ULID).

options.name: --title
options.description: Short title.

options.name: --objective
options.description: What the sponsor wants, in the sponsor's words.

options.name: --done
options.description: A completion condition as JSON; repeatable. A record predicate, {"type": ...} with optional subject, product, fields, state, min and max (or the same inside {"record": ...}), or an evidence statement, {"evidence": ..., "check": ...}.

options.name: --sponsor
options.description: The accountable principal; the proposer when omitted. A person who sponsors a goal activates and accepts it; a goal an agent sponsors is activated and accepted by an operator, and only an operator.

options.name: --delegate
options.description: A principal the sponsor, a person, delegates the acceptance of an ordinary goal to; it accepts while it holds the 'accept-work' scope, and never a goal that includes a reserved action.

options.name: --constraint
options.description: What must not change or happen; repeatable.

options.name: --budget
options.description: A cap its activation grants, unit=value; repeatable: wallMinutes and attemptsPerStep (both required), tokens, concurrency, or currency=<amount in minor units>:<unit> such as currency=5000:USD. A unit not given is not granted.

options.name: --roster
options.description: The roster record whose roles it uses; the estate's current roster when omitted.

options.name: --kind
options.description: finite (ends when done) or stewardship (holds a standing condition). [default: finite]

options.name: --work-order
options.description: A work order the sponsor gives as its plan; repeatable. Without one a planner proposes its work, as work orders that name the goal among their inputs.

options.name: --input
options.description: A record it builds on, as type:id; repeatable.

options.name: --deadline
options.description: The goal's deadline, for example 2026-12-01T00:00:00Z; validated and recorded but not yet enforced.

options.name: --supersedes
options.description: The goal this proposal revises, by its current revision's id; a revision needs a fresh activation, and only its sponsor, a person, or an operator for a goal an agent sponsors records it.

commands.name: activate
commands.description: Activate a proposed goal, which grants its budget: by its sponsor, a person who holds the operator role or a grant of the spending scope, or by an operator when an agent sponsors it. An agent never activates a goal.

options.name: --by
options.description: Acting principal id (ULID).

options.name: --note
options.description: Why, and what remains; a sentence naming the action when omitted.

commands.name: pause
commands.description: Pause an active goal; its sponsor's, or an operator's for a goal an agent sponsors. Prevents new runs but does not stop runs already in flight; use 'vericairn worker stop' for each run that must stop.

options.name: --by
options.description: Acting principal id (ULID).

options.name: --note
options.description: Why, and what remains; a sentence naming the action when omitted.

commands.name: resume
commands.description: Resume a paused, budget-limited or blocked goal, which grants its budget again; by whoever may activate it.

options.name: --by
options.description: Acting principal id (ULID).

options.name: --note
options.description: Why, and what remains; a sentence naming the action when omitted.

commands.name: stop
commands.description: Stop a goal: its sponsor, or an operator for a goal an agent sponsors, ends it as abandoned and prevents new runs. Runs already in flight are not stopped; use 'vericairn worker stop' for each run that must stop.

options.name: --by
options.description: Acting principal id (ULID).

options.name: --note
options.description: Why, and what remains; a sentence naming the action when omitted.

commands.name: custody-exception
commands.description: Record the sponsor's exception to the custody precondition for a goal's current revision: until it expires, a coding agent's run of the goal may launch unattended on a machine where a key of an operator or of the sponsor signs without its owner's presence, and the run names the exception. Recorded only by the goal's sponsor, or by an operator when an agent sponsors it; a revised goal needs a fresh one.

options.name: --by
options.description: Acting principal id (ULID).

options.name: --reason
options.description: Why unattended runs of the goal may launch while such a key signs where they run.

options.name: --expires
options.description: When the exception stops being in force, for example 2026-10-20T00:00:00Z.

commands.name: step
commands.description: Take a goal's next step, one at a time: its first eligible step whose route acts, routed from this machine by the goal's roster, for an operator, the goal's sponsor when a person, or a principal holding local-engineering. An agent's step goes on with the assignment that holds it, or is assigned to the agent with the run's intent, after the worker's whole preflight, and its run starts through the worker; every refusal before the intent records nothing, the assignment included, as while a key of an operator or of the sponsor signs here without presence and no custody exception is in force. A person's step is assigned to the person and asked of them, the two recorded together; a step no principal is available for is asked of the sponsor, never given to another contributor. It activates, funds, accepts and answers nothing.

options.name: --by
options.description: Acting principal id (ULID).

options.name: --repository
options.description: For an agent's step, the repository resource whose clone, registered on this machine (vericairn sources clone), its workspace is made from.

options.name: --setting
options.description: For an agent's step, a setting of the launcher routing chose, as name=value, for example command=<executable or JSON array>; repeatable.

options.name: --wall-minutes
options.description: For an agent's step, the run's cap in wall minutes; what remains of the goal's budget when omitted, and never more.

options.name: --branch
options.description: For an agent's step, the work branch; work/ and the work order's key when omitted.

options.name: --base
options.description: For an agent's step, what a new work branch starts from; the clone's HEAD when omitted.

options.name: --detach
options.description: Return once an agent's run is launched, leaving it to the daemon that serves the estate; without it the command waits until the run settles, and Ctrl+C asks it to stop. [default: False]

options.name: --configuration
options.description: Named local launcher configuration; required choices never fall back to ambient harness settings.

options.name: --execution
options.description: An explicit execution choice as name=value: model, effort, provider, destination, dataBoundary or adapter=disabled; repeatable. Inherited restrictions still apply.

options.name: --input-tokens
options.description: Context input allocation, within the run's token reservation; not measured consumption.

options.name: --output-tokens
options.description: Output allocation, within the run's token reservation; not measured consumption.

options.name: --context-bytes
options.description: Maximum canonical context payload bytes, separate from token reservations; mandatory originals and accounting must fit.

options.name: --context-package
options.description: Optional expected hash of the context package assembled for this run; a mismatch refuses dispatch.

arguments.name: GOAL
arguments.description: Goal record id (any revision); omit for the current goal.

commands.name: evaluate
commands.description: Record the evaluation of a goal's current revision, condition by condition, with the records each verdict read; by a principal other than any step's author.

options.name: --by
options.description: Acting principal id (ULID).

options.name: --summary
options.description: What was reviewed and how.

options.name: --verdict
options.description: A condition's verdict, n:verdict:reason with n from 1 and the verdict met, not-yet or impossible; repeatable. Every evidence statement needs one; a record predicate gets the runtime's, unless the evaluator judges one the runtime does not find met impossible.

options.name: --read
options.description: A record the evaluator read for a condition, n:record-id; repeatable. An evidence statement found met names at least one.

commands.name: accept
commands.description: Accept a goal at its current revision, relying on its current evaluation: by its sponsor when the sponsor is a person, or the principal the sponsor delegated an ordinary goal's acceptance to, and by an operator, only an operator, when an agent sponsors it; never by its evaluator or a step's author, and only once every condition is found met and every record predicate holds.

options.name: --by
options.description: Acting principal id (ULID).

options.name: --statement
options.description: What is accepted and on what basis.

commands.name: worker
commands.description: The worker (vericairn.worker/1): a coding agent carries one assignment toward its exit question through a launcher, in a workspace on a work branch, with its cap from its goal's budget recorded before it starts and its observed usage after. It accepts nothing; the agent's result is a claim another principal reviews.

commands.name: launchers
commands.description: List the coding-agent launchers available to the runtime, providers of vericairn.launcher.agent/1, with their settings and limitations.

commands.name: configure
commands.description: Show or replace this machine's workspace root, or a native launcher's configuration with --launcher. --workspaces sets an absolute root for every launcher. With no choices, show it; setting requires both model and effort and replaces the allowlists. Stored owner-only under VericairnHome, outside repositories; no secret values, commands or inventory additions. The CLI and daemon read it for each run; this command calls no API and runs no probes.

options.name: --launcher
options.description: The native launcher: codex or claude-code; omitted to show or set the workspace root.

options.name: --workspaces
options.description: Absolute machine-local workspace root for every launcher, outside repositories, estates and ancestors holding harness configuration. New roots are owner-only. Omit --launcher.

options.name: --model
options.description: Default portable model selector; required with --effort when setting.

options.name: --effort
options.description: Default effort in the launcher's native vocabulary; required with --model when setting.

options.name: --allow-model
options.description: Permitted model selector; repeatable, including the default. Omitted: only the default model.

options.name: --allow-effort
options.description: Permitted native effort; repeatable, including the default. Omitted: the launcher's supported efforts. Never expands its capabilities.

commands.name: qualify
commands.description: Record an authorized human's qualification of one exact installed harness version from local probe digests: version, help-confirmed flags, closed tools, isolated configuration, login boundary and effective MCP. It launches no agent, establishes no live inference or work acceptance, and grants no version range. Admission allows the shipped baseline or a current qualification whose repeated local probes have identical digests; a superseding record revokes the qualification. The existing inventory policy still applies. Remote is not built.

options.name: --launcher
options.description: The native launcher: codex or claude-code.

options.name: --by
options.description: A human operator or human explicitly granted the qualify scope; never an agent.

options.name: --setting
options.description: Local launcher setting as name=value, including command=<executable or JSON array>; repeatable. Values are never recorded.

commands.name: run
commands.description: Run a coding agent on an assignment: refused while the goal is not active or its budget is spent, while a device of an operator or the goal's sponsor signs here without presence and the sponsor recorded no custody exception in force for the goal, or when the launcher cannot run; otherwise the workspace is prepared, the intent recorded with the cap, the harness launched with the brief and the MCP server, observed, and its usage recorded once it exits.

options.name: --launcher
options.description: The launcher: claude-code, codex or generic (generic process launch is not complete agent support).

options.name: --agent
options.description: The agent principal the harness acts for: the assignment's contributor, with an admitted device whose key this machine holds.

options.name: --by
options.description: The principal recording the run: the operator, the goal's sponsor when the sponsor is a person, or a principal with the local-engineering scope.

options.name: --repository
options.description: The repository resource whose clone, registered on this machine (vericairn sources clone), the workspace is made from.

options.name: --goal
options.description: The goal the run is charged to, when the work belongs to more than one active goal.

options.name: --branch
options.description: The work branch; work/ and the work order's key when omitted. A later run of the branch continues in its workspace.

options.name: --base
options.description: What a new work branch starts from; the clone's HEAD when omitted.

options.name: --wall-minutes
options.description: The run's cap in wall minutes; what remains of the goal's budget when omitted, and never more.

options.name: --setting
options.description: A launcher setting as name=value, for example command=<executable or JSON array>; repeatable.

options.name: --detach
options.description: Return once the harness is launched, leaving the run to the daemon that serves the estate; without it the command waits until the run settles, and Ctrl+C asks it to stop. [default: False]

options.name: --configuration
options.description: Named local launcher configuration; required choices never fall back to ambient harness settings.

options.name: --execution
options.description: An explicit execution choice as name=value: model, effort, provider, destination, dataBoundary or adapter=disabled; repeatable. Inherited restrictions still apply.

options.name: --input-tokens
options.description: Context input allocation, within the run's token reservation; not measured consumption.

options.name: --output-tokens
options.description: Output allocation, within the run's token reservation; not measured consumption.

options.name: --context-bytes
options.description: Maximum canonical context payload bytes, separate from token reservations; mandatory originals and accounting must fit.

options.name: --context-package
options.description: Optional expected hash of the context package assembled for this run; a mismatch refuses dispatch.

arguments.name: ASSIGNMENT
arguments.description: The assignment the agent carries, whose contributor it is.

commands.name: stop
commands.description: Ask a run to stop and report what was observed: the request, its transmission to the harness, the harness's acknowledgment, an escalation after the grace period and the containment, each only once observed. A stop that is not observed is reported as requested.

options.name: --by
options.description: The principal asking for the stop.

options.name: --reason
options.description: Why.

options.name: --grace
options.description: Seconds the harness has to stop once the stop is transmitted before its process tree is killed; the worker's default, ten, when omitted.

arguments.name: RUN
arguments.description: The run: its id, the id of any of its operation's revisions, or its identity.

commands.name: runs
commands.description: List the agent runs with their caps, their observed usage, what each is charged (its cap for what was not reported, and while in flight) and their stops, and the ledgers of their goals.

commands.name: devices
commands.description: Device keys: create a device for a principal on this machine, pair one on another machine, list, admit, revoke, rename and rotate, and the operator's recovery device.

commands.name: create
commands.description: Generate a key on this machine and record the device, signed by its own key.

options.name: --principal
options.description: The principal this device acts for.

options.name: --name
options.description: Descriptive device name, never a machine path.

options.name: --custody
options.description: Key custody: default, the strongest this machine offers (CNG on Windows; the Secure Enclave on a Mac that has one; the secret service on Linux where one runs; else an owner-only file), or file, cng, secure-enclave or secret-service.

options.name: --presence
options.description: Every signature needs its owner's presence (Touch ID or the login password; Secure Enclave custody only, never for an agent). Default: a person's device needs it wherever its custody enforces it; '--presence false' declines.

options.name: --profile
options.description: Permitted connectivity profile; repeatable (default: embedded).

commands.name: list
commands.description: List device records with their admission state and whether their key is held here.

commands.name: admit
commands.description: Admit a device to author records in this estate (operator or 'administer' scope).

options.name: --by
options.description: Authoring principal id (ULID).

options.name: --note
options.description: Why the device is admitted.

options.name: --recovery
options.description: Sign with the operator's recovery key in this file, when no admitted device of the operator is left; asks for its passphrase. Every use stays in 'status' until the operator reviews it.

options.name: --passphrase-stdin
options.description: Read the recovery key's passphrase from the first line of standard input instead of the terminal. [default: False]

commands.name: revoke
commands.description: Revoke a device's admission from now on; its earlier records stay attributable.

options.name: --by
options.description: Authoring principal id (ULID).

options.name: --reason
options.description: Why the admission ends.

options.name: --recovery
options.description: Sign with the operator's recovery key in this file, when no admitted device of the operator is left; asks for its passphrase. Every use stays in 'status' until the operator reviews it.

options.name: --passphrase-stdin
options.description: Read the recovery key's passphrase from the first line of standard input instead of the terminal. [default: False]

commands.name: recovery
commands.description: Make the operator's recovery device for emergency access: its key is written once to a file, encrypted with a passphrase you type, and never held by this machine; an admitted device of the operator held here admits it (record format 2).

options.name: --principal
options.description: The operator the recovery device acts for.

options.name: --name
options.description: Descriptive name, for example where the key is kept; never a machine path.

options.name: --output
options.description: New file to write the encrypted key to, outside the estate's repository; move it off this machine at once.

options.name: --passphrase-stdin
options.description: Read the recovery key's passphrase from the first line of standard input instead of the terminal. [default: False]

commands.name: pair
commands.description: Issue a pairing code for a new device on another machine: 16 characters, valid ten minutes, for one device and five attempts. Entered there with 'vericairn connections add', it records the device with the key it presents and admits it under your authority (needs the runtime serving the local-network profile).

options.name: --principal
options.description: The principal the new device will act for.

options.name: --by
options.description: The administrator: the operator, or a principal holding the 'administer' scope, whose admitted device on this machine signs the admission.

options.name: --profile
options.description: A connectivity profile the device will be permitted; repeatable (default: local-network).

commands.name: writes
commands.description: List what paired devices wrote over the local network through this machine's runtime: when, which device, for which principal, the operation and the record it produced. A record a paired device asks for is signed by a device of the same principal held here, so this is where the paired device behind it is kept.

arguments.name: DEVICE
arguments.description: A paired device's id, to list its writes only.

commands.name: rename
commands.description: Rename a device whose key is held here; it keeps its identity, key and admission (record format 2).

options.name: --name
options.description: The device's new descriptive name, never a machine path.

commands.name: rotate
commands.description: Replace a device's key with a new one, signed by both keys; the device keeps its identity and admission, and its earlier records stay valid (record format 2).

options.name: --custody
options.description: Custody of the new key: file, cng, secure-enclave, secret-service, or default for the strongest this machine offers (when omitted: the custody the device has).

options.name: --presence
options.description: Every signature with the new key needs its owner's presence (Secure Enclave custody only, never for an agent); '--presence false' removes it. Default: the device's presence, where the new custody enforces it.

commands.name: connections
commands.description: The runtimes this machine reaches over the local network: add one by pairing with a code, list them with their state, and remove one. Kept for this user on this machine, never in a repository.

commands.name: add
commands.description: Pair this machine with the runtime at an address using a code an administrator issued: the runtime proves it knows the code and who it is, this machine makes its device key and presents it, and the runtime records and admits the device. The connection pins the runtime's identity.

options.name: --code
options.description: The pairing code, as shown: four groups of four characters (16 in all).

options.name: --name
options.description: This device's descriptive name, never a machine path.

options.name: --custody
options.description: Key custody: default, the strongest this machine offers, or file, cng, secure-enclave or secret-service.

options.name: --presence
options.description: Every signature needs its owner's presence (Secure Enclave custody only, never for an agent). Default: a person's device needs it wherever its custody enforces it; '--presence false' declines.

arguments.name: ADDRESS
arguments.description: Where the runtime listens: its address and port, as the pairing code's administrator gave them, for example 192.168.1.20:7443.

commands.name: list
commands.description: Check every connection now and show its state: current, partial, denied, cached (with when it was last current) or unavailable.

commands.name: remove
commands.description: Forget a connection on this machine. The device stays admitted until an administrator revokes it, since disconnection is never revocation, and its key stays in this machine's custody.

commands.name: release
commands.description: Releases: list the records and the providers, submit a release through the provider its product declares or the request names as intent before effect, observe the run, the draft and the publication.

commands.name: list
commands.description: List current release records: version, status, commit, id, signing.

commands.name: providers
commands.description: List the provider and adapter implementations available to the runtime, with the settings each declares and its defaults.

commands.name: submit
commands.description: Record the intent, then dispatch the build through the provider; the run id and outcome are recorded as they are observed. Never publishes.

options.name: --product
options.description: Product record id the release belongs to; its declared release destination supplies the provider and settings the request does not name.

options.name: --version
options.description: The version to release, for example 0.4.0.

options.name: --by
options.description: Principal id recording the operation (ULID).

options.name: --provider
options.description: The provider id, for example github-releases; the product's declared provider when omitted.

options.name: --repository
options.description: The setting repository (for GitHub, owner/name of the repository whose workflow builds the release).

options.name: --ref
options.description: The setting ref (the branch or tag to build from); the provider's default when omitted.

options.name: --workflow
options.description: The setting workflow (the release workflow file); the provider's default when omitted.

options.name: --setting
options.description: Any declared setting as name=value; repeatable.

options.name: --reconciliation
options.description: How an earlier failed, canceled or uncertain attempt under the same identity was settled; required for a retry.

commands.name: observe
commands.description: Observe the run and the draft through the provider the operation records; record the outcome, the candidate release, and later the operator's manual publication.

options.name: --version
options.description: The version to release, for example 0.4.0.

options.name: --by
options.description: Principal id recording the operation (ULID).

options.name: --product
options.description: Product record id, to find the operation by product and version.

options.name: --provider
options.description: The provider id, for example github-releases; the product's declared provider when omitted.

options.name: --repository
options.description: The setting repository (for GitHub, owner/name of the repository whose workflow builds the release).

options.name: --qualified
options.description: Platform whose qualification is recorded for the candidate; repeatable.

options.name: --limitation
options.description: A known limitation of the candidate; repeatable.

options.name: --signing
options.description: Signing state recorded on the candidate. [default: unsigned developer build]

options.name: --cancel
options.description: Settle an intent that was never dispatched, or an outcome reconciled as having had no effect, with this reason.

commands.name: sources
commands.description: Repositories the estate uses: inspect read-only, adopt as a resource, observe again, and register this machine's clone.

commands.name: inspect
commands.description: Observe a repository read-only: commit, branch, remote, working-tree state, tags, recent history.

arguments.name: PATH
arguments.description: Path of a git working tree on this machine; never recorded.

commands.name: adopt
commands.description: Adopt a repository as a resource by observation: a resource record and a first observation; nothing in the repository changes.

options.name: --by
options.description: Authoring principal id (ULID).

options.name: --name
options.description: Display name of the resource.

options.name: --role
options.description: What the estate uses the repository for.

options.name: --visibility
options.description: public, private or n/a. [default: private]

options.name: --notes
options.description: Free text.

arguments.name: PATH
arguments.description: Path of a git working tree on this machine; never recorded.

commands.name: observe
commands.description: Record a fresh observation of an adopted repository.

options.name: --resource
options.description: Resource record id of the adopted repository.

options.name: --by
options.description: Authoring principal id (ULID).

arguments.name: PATH
arguments.description: Path of a git working tree on this machine; never recorded.

commands.name: clone
commands.description: Register this machine's clone of an adopted repository, so that living documents in it can be read at a commit; the path is machine configuration, never a record.

options.name: --resource
options.description: Resource record id of the adopted repository.

arguments.name: PATH
arguments.description: Path of a git working tree on this machine; never recorded.

commands.name: check
commands.description: Run a check and record its evidence as a verification of the exact commit, or observe a workflow run.

commands.name: run
commands.description: Run a command in a repository and record a verification: commit, command, environment, exit code, duration and output as evidence.

options.name: --resource
options.description: Resource record id of the repository checked.

options.name: --by
options.description: Authoring principal id (ULID).

options.name: --in
options.description: Working tree the command runs in. [default: <path>]

options.name: --role
options.description: self, independent-agent, operator or automation. [default: self]

options.name: --summary
options.description: What the check establishes, in your words; the observed exit and duration are recorded regardless.

options.name: --timeout
options.description: Seconds after which the command is stopped and its result recorded as unknown. [default: 3600]

arguments.name: COMMAND
arguments.description: The command and its arguments; put -- before it.

commands.name: observe
commands.description: Observe a workflow run at its host and record it as automation's verification of the commit it built.

options.name: --resource
options.description: Resource record id of the repository checked.

options.name: --repository
options.description: Where the run is (for GitHub, owner/name); the resource's recorded location when omitted.

options.name: --provider
options.description: The provider that observes the run; the one serving the resource's recorded location when omitted.

options.name: --run
options.description: Workflow run id.

options.name: --workflow
options.description: Workflow file the run belongs to. [default: ci.yml]

options.name: --by
options.description: Authoring principal id (ULID).

commands.name: runtime
commands.description: The daemon that owns an estate's live state on this machine: serve, start, stop, status, install, uninstall, configure (the local-network profile) and rotate (its certificate).

commands.name: serve
commands.description: Serve the estate in this process until stopped (Ctrl+C or 'runtime stop'); refuses when a daemon already serves it.

options.name: --no-loopback
options.description: Disable the pinned loopback TLS endpoint. The local socket and any configured local-network listener remain available. [default: False]

options.name: --detached
options.description: Write the daemon's output to its log beside the estate's live store instead of the standard streams; 'runtime start' serves this way. [default: False]

commands.name: start
commands.description: Start a daemon for the estate in the background and wait until it answers.

commands.name: stop
commands.description: Ask the daemon serving the estate to stop; closing a client never stops it.

commands.name: status
commands.description: Whether a daemon serves the estate and where, or whether commands run the embedded runtime.

commands.name: install
commands.description: Install the daemon as a per-user service that starts at login (launchd agent, systemd user unit or a logon task).

options.name: --plan
options.description: Show the unit and the commands without installing anything. [default: False]

commands.name: uninstall
commands.description: Remove the per-user service installed by 'runtime install'.

commands.name: configure
commands.description: Configure the runtime of this estate on this machine; without options, show the configuration. Nothing listens beyond the local socket and loopback unless an address is set.

options.name: --local-network
options.description: The address and port the local-network profile listens on from the runtime's next start, an IP address of this machine such as 192.168.1.20:7443; 'off' turns it off. Off unless set.

options.name: --allow-public
options.description: With --local-network, allow a wildcard address (every interface) or one other networks can reach; such an address is refused without it. [default: False]

commands.name: rotate
commands.description: Replace the runtime certificate now (it is also replaced on a schedule before it expires). Paired devices keep working, since they pin the runtime identity, which signs the certificate in use; loopback clients read the new one from the endpoint file.

options.name: --compromised
options.description: The certificate's key may be known to someone else: also close every open connection, so nothing continues under it. [default: False]

options.name: --identity
options.description: The runtime identity's key may be known to someone else: replace the identity too; every paired device then pairs again. [default: False]

options.name: --reason
options.description: Why, for the runtime's log.

commands.name: recover
commands.description: After an interruption or a move: inspect what this copy holds and compare it with another.

commands.name: inspect
commands.description: What this copy knows, which devices can author from here, work in progress, unresolved effects and reconcile tasks.

commands.name: compare
commands.description: Records only in this copy, only in the other, or (never expected) differing in content.

options.name: --with
options.description: Root of the other copy.

commands.name: objects
commands.description: Content-addressed objects: put, list, verify.

commands.name: put
commands.description: Store a file's bytes as an object named by their hash.

arguments.name: FILE
arguments.description: File whose bytes become an object.

commands.name: list
commands.description: List held objects.

commands.name: verify
commands.description: Read every object and check its bytes against its name.

commands.name: docs
commands.description: Documentation: a release's set (its notes from the estate's records, and the check that a set holds every document its manifest lists; the references are generated by the product's own build tooling), and the living documents that stay true as the estate changes.

commands.name: notes
commands.description: Write release notes from the estate's records since the previous release's notes ended, and record their window in the set's manifest.

options.name: --from
options.description: The earlier published release's version; the notes begin where the notes of its documentation set, the directory it names beside --out, ended (at its publication when there is no such set).

options.name: --to
options.description: The release's version; its publication ends the notes once it is recorded, the second before they are generated until then.

options.name: --out
options.description: Directory of the documentation set the notes belong to.

options.name: --since
options.description: The time the notes begin, for example 2026-10-16T04:29:43Z, no later than the previous set's end; widens the window to include records the previous set missed and records the chosen start in the manifest.

commands.name: check
commands.description: Refuse a documentation set that lacks a document, or a heading for a command, an API operation or a record type its manifest lists; every gap is listed at once.

options.name: --documents
options.description: The product's declaration of the documents every set holds (a JSON array of file names); the set's manifest is checked against it.

commands.name: living
commands.description: List the declared living documents: each one current, due with every trigger newer than its latest clearance, or unavailable.

commands.name: review
commands.description: Record a review of a living document: the runtime reads its content, records the covered paths' identity and the triggers it answers, and runs its declared checks; a failed check refuses the clearance.

options.name: --by
options.description: The reviewing principal (ULID).

options.name: --outcome
options.description: current (it holds), revised (it was changed for the trigger) or needs-change (it is stale and stays due).

options.name: --summary
options.description: What was checked.

options.name: --finding
options.description: A finding, severity:summary with severity error, warning or info; repeatable.

options.name: --commit
options.description: For a document of another repository, the commit reviewed.

options.name: --independence
options.description: For a document of another repository, whose author the estate's records do not show, the reviewer's independence of its content: self (the reviewer wrote or revised it), independent-agent or operator. Default: self for a principal that holds the builder role, else judged from the estate's records. An estate file's revisions decide its reviewer's independence, and a statement that differs is refused.

commands.name: declare
commands.description: Record or revise the declaration of a living document: its triggers and levels, generated regions, checks and who may clear it.

options.name: --by
options.description: Authoring principal id (ULID).

options.name: --body
options.description: Path to a JSON file holding the living-document declaration, or '-' for standard input.

options.name: --supersedes
options.description: The declaration this one revises.

commands.name: regenerate
commands.description: Rewrite an estate document's generated regions, or a generated document, from their generators; nothing outside the markers changes.

commands.name: mcp
commands.description: The Model Context Protocol server: serve the estate to a coding agent over standard input and output, or generate the agent orientation files.

commands.name: serve
commands.description: Serve the estate's tools over standard input and output until the input ends; a client of the daemon or the embedded runtime, never a second owner.

options.name: --as
options.description: Principal id the agent acts for; its admitted device on this machine signs the writes. Without it only the read-only tools are listed.

commands.name: orientation
commands.description: Write AGENTS.md and the pointer files for the common agent harnesses from the estate's identity, its qualifications of agent harnesses and the tool registry, or check existing copies against a fresh generation.

options.name: --out
options.description: Directory to write the files into, for example a repository root.

options.name: --as
options.description: Principal id the files describe as the acting principal, if any.

options.name: --check
options.description: Write nothing; compare the files in --out with a fresh generation and name every one that is missing or differs. [default: False]

commands.name: context
commands.description: Prepare measured context and retrieve pinned originals under current permission.

commands.name: catalogue
commands.description: List the current document revision catalogue without selecting or reading its bodies.

commands.name: prepare
commands.description: Compute the context package for a work order without writing.

options.name: --max-bytes
options.description: Remaining context input allocation in bytes, separate from the run spending cap. Mandatory overflow is refused.

commands.name: read
commands.description: Read and verify a pinned original, never silently its latest revision.

options.name: --source
options.description: Legacy manifest handles are unavailable; prepare context again for a pin.

options.name: --original
options.description: Return only the pinned original. [default: False]

options.name: --out
options.description: Write exact bytes to a new file; never overwrite.

arguments.name: PIN
arguments.description: Self-contained pinned identity from the package.

commands.name: updates
commands.description: Machine-local release check settings shared by the CLI and Workbench; nothing installs or upgrades automatically.

commands.name: configure
commands.description: Show this machine's release check setting, or replace it with --enabled true or false. Enabled by default; the check is unauthenticated and carries no identifiers or usage telemetry. Settings and the timestamped cache stay under VericairnHome/updates, outside repositories and estates. Disabling makes no request and retains the cached answer. This command itself never checks the network.

options.name: --enabled
options.description: Whether to check for published releases at most once per 24 hours, including failed attempts. False prevents requests; true enables future checks. Omit to show the setting.

commands.name: status
commands.description: Show the estate's current state derived from its records, with compact required attention resolved from current evidence. Each item names its exact source and inspection command. --json is identical on every machine for the same records and includes complete record-derived attention references. Human status also shows labelled local worker concerns. Discloses and checks GitHub for a newer published release at most once per 24 hours, shared with Workbench; no identifiers or usage telemetry. Disclosure and upgrade notices go to stderr, leaving stdout and JSON unchanged. Disable with vericairn updates configure --enabled false. Offline failures keep the cached answer and never fail this command.

options.name: --observe
options.description: Explicitly record that a person observed status; requires --by. Ordinary reads record nothing. [default: False]

options.name: --by
options.description: The observing human principal; used only with --observe.

commands.name: progress
commands.description: Show the estate's recorded progress with latest local agent claims and worker observations labelled separately: where the estate stands, the work orders by state, each published release and what it contained, what comes next by release, the next eligible work and what waits on the operator. Required attention names only open obligations with exact references and inspection commands; ordinary after ordering is planning. --json includes complete attention references.

commands.name: resume
commands.description: Show every record, pin and observed-state change since a retained hand-over. The world may have moved; this restarts nothing.

arguments.name: PACKAGE
arguments.description: The retained hand-over JSON file, or - for standard input.

commands.name: handoff
commands.description: Prepare a complete record-derived hand-over; refuse missing sources or overflow. Remote is not built.

options.name: --out
options.description: Retain the portable package in a new file; never overwrite.

options.name: --max-bytes
options.description: Optional payload byte limit; no truncation. No limit when omitted.

commands.name: ask
commands.description: Show what waits on a principal, or on every principal: the asks still open or notified, at most three in one delivery with the recommendation first and the consequence of leaving each unanswered, the rest waiting in order. Reading them answers nothing; an ask is answered by a decision of the principal it is put to that names it in its answers.

options.name: --to
options.description: The principal asked (ULID); every principal when omitted.

commands.name: decisions
commands.description: List the estate's current decisions, or show one cleanly.

arguments.name: ID
arguments.description: Decision record id (any revision); omit to list.

commands.name: doctor
commands.description: Check this machine's prerequisites. Discloses and checks GitHub for a newer published release at most once per 24 hours, shared with Workbench; no identifiers or usage telemetry. Disclosure and upgrade notices go to stderr, leaving stdout and JSON unchanged. Disable with vericairn updates configure --enabled false. Offline failures keep the cached answer and never fail this command.

commands.name: version
commands.description: Print the version. Discloses and checks GitHub for a newer published release at most once per 24 hours, shared with Workbench; no identifiers or usage telemetry. Disclosure and upgrade notices go to stderr, leaving stdout and JSON unchanged. Disable with vericairn updates configure --enabled false. Offline failures keep the cached answer and never fail this command.
